standard_prerequisites: the localization functor epsilon^* from O_X-modules to O_etale-modules on the small etale site and its flatness
RSheafHom in the derived category of modules on a ringed site
pseudo-coherent and perfect complexes represented by finite free resp. strictly perfect complexes
the Rhom representation lemmas for complexes of direct summands of finite free modules and for strictly perfect complexes
core_obligations: Prove the canonical isomorphism epsilon^* RSheafHom(E,F) to RSheafHom(epsilon^*E, epsilon^*F) when E is pseudo-coherent and F bounded below, or E is perfect and F arbitrary
proof_roadmap: Flatness of epsilon makes epsilon^* the derived pullback, and the fancy base change remark gives the canonical map

Case (1): represent E by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and F by a bounded below complex; the two Rhom-complex representation lemmas identify both sides with direct sums of SheafHoms, reducing the claim to the pointwise fact that epsilon^* SheafHom(E,F) to SheafHom(epsilon^*E, epsilon^*F) is an isomorphism for finite free E
Case (2): represent E by a strictly perfect complex via the affine comparison lemmas for perfect complexes and repeat the same argument with the strictly perfect Rhom representation lemma
difficulty_reason: H2: a two-case representation argument reducing a derived-level base change to the finite-free pointwise isomorphism; the source writes both cases in full.
